sections.title: Letter sound erre
paragraphs: The letter (erre) /ˈɛʁi/ mainly makes the sound /ʁ/, as in the word (rua) /ˈʁu.ɐ/, which means street. In European Portuguese, this letter can make two distinct sounds.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: For the first sound, lift the back of your tongue near the soft roof of your mouth. Let the air scrape gently past while your voice hums. For the second sound, tap the tip of your tongue once quickly against the ridge behind your upper front teeth. Touch your throat to feel your voice buzz during both sounds.

sections.title: Spelling and sounds
paragraphs: At the start of a word, this letter makes the sound /ʁ/, as in (carro) /ˈka.ʁu/. Between two vowels, it makes the tapped sound /ɾ/, as in (caro) /ˈka.ɾu/. At the end of a syllable, it also makes the sound /ɾ/, as in (porta) /ˈpɔɾ.tɐ/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not roll your tongue tip like the Spanish sound. Do not curl your tongue backward like the sound in the English word red. Keep your tongue flat for the back sound, or tap it once quickly against your upper gum for the light tap.
